# Strange Canada

> Strange Canada is a roadside oddities atlas of Canada: giant statues, strange museums, UFO landing pads, ghost towns, and mysterious places you can actually drive to. Every attraction is a real place, written about affectionately and checked against primary sources; "world's largest" figures are the towns' own claims, reported as such. Facts on each article were last verified on the date shown in its schema.

## Main sections

- [Home](https://strangecanada.ca/): the latest field notes and featured stops
- [Articles](https://strangecanada.ca/articles/): every field note, newest first
- [Oddities Atlas](https://strangecanada.ca/atlas/): every strange stop on one map of Canada
- [About](https://strangecanada.ca/about/): what Strange Canada is and how we check our facts
- [Contact](https://strangecanada.ca/contact/): suggest a stop or report a change

## Flagship field notes

- [Mac the Moose](https://strangecanada.ca/articles/mac-the-moose/): Moose Jaw, Saskatchewan's 10-tonne moose (1984) and the Moose War with Norway's Storelgen
- [The Giant Perogy of Glendon](https://strangecanada.ca/articles/the-giant-perogy-of-glendon/): a roughly 27-foot perogy on a fork in Glendon, Alberta (1991)
- [The UFO Landing Pad of St. Paul](https://strangecanada.ca/articles/the-ufo-landing-pad-of-st-paul/): the landing pad St. Paul, Alberta built as a 1967 Centennial project
- [Falcon Lake: Canada's Strangest UFO Story](https://strangecanada.ca/articles/falcon-lake-ufo/): Stefan Michalak's reported 1967 encounter in Manitoba's Whiteshell, told as a reported account
- [The Big Nickel](https://strangecanada.ca/articles/the-big-nickel-sudbury/): Sudbury, Ontario's nine-metre stainless-steel nickel (1964) at Dynamic Earth
- [The Sign Post Forest](https://strangecanada.ca/articles/sign-post-forest-watson-lake/): Watson Lake, Yukon's forest of signs, begun by a homesick soldier in 1942
- [Magnetic Hill](https://strangecanada.ca/articles/magnetic-hill-moncton/): Moncton, New Brunswick's famous gravity illusion, rolling cars uphill since the 1930s
- [The World's Largest Lobster](https://strangecanada.ca/articles/worlds-largest-lobster-shediac/): Shediac, New Brunswick's giant lobster (1990), the town's "world's largest" claim
- [Happy Rock](https://strangecanada.ca/articles/happy-rock-gladstone/): Gladstone, Manitoba's grinning 36-foot rock (1993)
- [The World's Largest Curling Rock](https://strangecanada.ca/articles/worlds-largest-curling-rock-arborg/): Arborg, Manitoba's giant curling rock (2005), 4.2 metres across, honouring its champion high school teams — the town's "world's largest" claim
- [The Giant Mosquito of Komarno](https://strangecanada.ca/articles/giant-mosquito-komarno/): Komarno, Manitoba's giant mosquito (1986), 4.6 metres long and a working weathervane, honouring a community name that means lots of mosquitos — the town's "world's largest" claim
- [Chasing Ghosts in BC's Interior](https://strangecanada.ca/articles/chasing-ghosts-in-bcs-interior/): the ghost towns of Sandon, Barkerville, and Phoenix, British Columbia

## En français

Strange Canada est aussi publié intégralement en français (pages réelles, pas de traduction automatique) :

- [Accueil en français](https://strangecanada.ca/fr/) : les plus récentes notes de terrain
- [Articles en français](https://strangecanada.ca/fr/articles/) : toutes les notes de terrain en français
- [L'atlas des curiosités](https://strangecanada.ca/fr/atlas/) : tous les arrêts étranges sur une seule carte
- [À propos](https://strangecanada.ca/fr/about/) : ce qu'est Strange Canada et comment nous vérifions nos faits
- [La plus grande pierre de curling au monde](https://strangecanada.ca/fr/articles/worlds-largest-curling-rock-arborg/) : la pierre de curling géante d'Arborg, au Manitoba (2005), 4,2 mètres de large, en l'honneur de ses équipes scolaires championnes — la revendication de la ville
- [Le moustique géant de Komarno](https://strangecanada.ca/fr/articles/giant-mosquito-komarno/) : le moustique géant de Komarno, au Manitoba (1986), 4,6 mètres de long et girouette fonctionnelle, en l'honneur d'un nom de communauté qui veut dire plein de moustiques — la revendication de la ville
